recorded: Every case passed against the original in each of 3 runs, with Node.js 26.12.1, @langchain/core 1.1.19, @langchain/langgraph 1.1.4, @langchain/mcp-adapters 1.1.3, @langchain/openai 1.2.7, langchain 1.2.17, zod 4.3.6, imported as zod/v3, and @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem 2026.1.14, installed from the module's lockfile and run as "node src/index.ts" without a .env file, which the npm scripts require through --env-file. The original always calls OpenRouter's address, so the copy that produced these cases reads OPENAI_BASE_URL first and falls back to it, a one-line change in src/services/openrouterService.ts. No OpenRouter key was available, so the answers were recorded from Ollama 0.40.11 through its OpenAI-compatible API, with gpt-oss:20b standing in for both qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct and openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b, and wrapped in OpenRouter's documented response format without the stand-in's reasoning, while the requests keep the models and the routing the program sends. The stand-in judged the admin's plain question unsafe in both recordings, because the guardrail reads the system prompt and its security rules before the message, so that verdict has a case of its own, and the SAFE verdict that lets the admin through is synthesized in the guardrails prompt's format, followed by the agent's answers from a run with --unsafe, whose chat requests are the same. In that run, the stand-in first passed null for read_text_file's optional head and tail, which the tool's schema rejected, so the replay leaves that attempt out and continues with the call that followed it. The stand-in refused the member's maintenance mode injection with --unsafe, which qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct, the model the lesson marks as unsafe, follows, so that case's tool call and answer are synthesized, and the answer only reports package.json's version. No case reads .env. Ollama, shared with other recordings at the time, answered nothing for 15 minutes, so the verdicts on the braces and on the role-play prompt file and the answer to the user from the written users file are synthesized as well. So are the two verdicts that test the prefix rule, one in lower case after blank lines and one that names UNSAFE after its start, and the two rejected calls, which follow OpenRouter's documented error format. The cases where the agent reads package.json write the lesson's own package.json first, so the tool finds version 1.2.0 in any transcription's folder, and they check the tool message by the package's name and version, whether it holds the file's text or the MCP text block around it. The filesystem MCP server starts through npx, the lockfile's version for the original and possibly the latest elsewhere, so the cases check its tools by name only, and its standard error and npm's notices pass through, so the cases with the agent only require standard error to hold neither node's error. max_tokens is not compared, because clients send it as max_tokens or max_completion_tokens. The usage line names npm run chat, so the cases check only the rest of that line, and the runtime's own errors after Guardrails check failed:, Chat node error:, and Fatal error: are checked as any non-empty text, the last one only to name the file. The LangGraph CLI's development server, which factory.ts and langgraph.json register the graph for, belongs to the CLI and has no cases, and neither has the chat node's fallback to ananeri with the guardrails off, which only a state without a user reaches.
